meta.title: Quickstart: streaming · {brand}
meta.description: Stream samples from a lab PC to the platform through the encrypted write-ahead buffer.

heading: Stream from a lab PC.
lede: Samples go into an encrypted buffer on disk first and are sent from there. A slow or unreachable network never stops acquisition; after a disconnect the SDK resumes from what the server has stored.

sections.heading: Register the device key
body: The device signs every chunk. The private key is generated inside the SDK core and cannot be exported; on Windows it can be kept sealed by the operating system with DeviceKey.sealed(path). Only the public key is sent.

sections.heading: Open a stream
body: Streams carry the data direction device to platform only; nothing is ever sent to acquisition hardware.

The SDK cuts and signs chunks by time, using the sampling rate you register: chunk_ms sets the chunk length (default 100 ms, minimum 20 ms, so a 30 kHz stream is never signed per sample). The last, shorter chunk is written when you drain, and it ends the stream.

lines: channels = [{"name": f"EEG{i:02d}", "modality": "EEG", "units": "uV"} for i in range(8)]

sections.heading: Push samples with their timestamps
body: Each sample keeps its original timestamp. Clock offsets are stored next to the samples exactly as measured; corrections are separate derived data.

sections.heading: Drain and close
body: drain waits until the server has acknowledged every buffered chunk; acknowledged chunks are deleted from the buffer. finish closes the stream on the server.

sections.heading: From an LSL stream
body: {pkg}.lsl.LslInlet reads an existing LSL stream (inlet only) and captures LSL clock offsets with their reported uncertainty. Pass it to streaming.run_acquisition together with a stream. This path runs in CI with a test outlet; it is not part of this quickstart because it needs an LSL source.
